data.providerPathway: Supported: an NBCC Approved Continuing Education Provider (or affiliate) is expressly an approved sponsor for counselor CE under 68 IAC 1375.220(c)(1)(A). Courses must be counseling/clinical-counseling relevant and satisfy the rule's content, qualified-presenter, objectives/methods, evaluation, examination, and certificate requirements; the rule does not limit this pathway to particular courses.
data.asyncRule: Accepted: remote courses may be live or recorded, including pre-recorded online, computer, mail, or live online courses, but must be offered by an approved sponsor and include an examination. Thus asynchronous home study is accepted when these conditions are met.
data.limits: 30 CE hours per 24-month renewal period; at least 3 ethics hours. One CE hour is 50 minutes; after the initial hour, credit may be in half-hour increments. No separate cap stated for remote/home-study courses. LCPC second renewal has a one-time 9-hour clinical-supervision requirement.
data.passage: 68 IAC 1375.220(c)(1)(A): “National Board for Certified Counselors or its affiliates”; 1375.220(b)(2): “Remote courses may be live or recorded ... pre-recorded online course/program ... Each course shall include an examination”; 1375.220(c)(3)(A)-(E): courses must advance professional skills, be presented by persons educated/experienced in the subject, specify objectives/content/methods, and hours; 1375.220(a)(4): “One CE hour shall equal 50 minutes of attendance.”

data.providerPathway: Conditional: NBCC approval alone is not named as an LMFT sponsor pathway. An NBCC provider would need Illinois Division approval/authorization as a CE sponsor under 68 IAC 1283.110(c)(1)-(2) (unless otherwise qualifying through the listed AAMFT pathway). Courses must be marriage-and-family-therapy relevant and meet the program, presenter, objectives/content/methods, evaluation, examination, and certificate standards.
data.asyncRule: Accepted conditionally: distance learning expressly includes pre-recorded online, live online, mail, and computer courses, provided by an approved sponsor, and each course must include an examination.
data.limits: 30 CE hours per 24-month pre-renewal period; one CE hour is 50 minutes. No separate asynchronous/home-study cap stated. First Illinois renewal is exempt.
data.passage: 68 IAC 1283.110(b)(5): “CE hours may be earned through completion of a distance learning course (e.g., pre-recorded online course/program, live online course/program, by mail, computer, etc.) that is offered by an approved sponsor ... Each such course shall include an examination”; 1283.110(c)(1): sponsor means AAMFT and “any other” person/group “approved and authorized by the Division”; 1283.110(a)(3): “One CE hour shall equal 50 minutes.”

data.providerPathway: Conditional: NBCC approval alone is not listed as an approved social-work sponsor. An NBCC provider must separately be an Illinois-approved CE sponsor (or otherwise fall within the listed sponsor categories); the sponsor must meet Illinois course-material, qualified-presenter, content/objective/method, evaluation, completion-certificate, and record requirements. Courses must be relevant to social work/clinical social work.
data.asyncRule: Accepted conditionally: remote programs expressly include self-study, book-study, and computer/online courses, but they must be offered by an approved sponsor and include an examination. No separate asynchronous cap stated.
data.limits: 30 CE hours per renewal period, including at least 3 ethics hours and at least 3 cultural-competence hours. The rule specifies remote completion but does not state a separate home-study cap or a different hour conversion. Beginning the renewal period ending Nov. 30, 2027, certain LCSWs have a one-time 6-hour clinical-supervision requirement.
data.passage: 68 IAC 1470.95(b)(2): “CE credit also may be earned by verified completion ... of a remote program (e.g., self-study, book-study, or computer/online based course) that is offered by an approved sponsor ... Each remote course shall include an examination”; 1470.95(c)(2)(A)-(C): sponsor submits a CE program/course materials for review and verifies completion/certificates; 1470.95(a)(1): 30 hours, including ethics and cultural competence.

data.providerPathway: Conditional: Iowa's current behavioral-health rule does not name NBCC-approved providers as an automatic provider pathway. CE is creditable when the activity meets the general standards (organized learning directly contributing to competency; practice-related subject matter; qualified presenters; stated objectives; and sponsor-issued proof/certificate).
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous/home-study is accepted as an 'independent study course' if it meets the general criteria in 481—881.2(9), including a posttest under the rule's definition of independent study. No separate numerical cap on independent-study/home-study hours is stated; the ordinary biennial requirement is 40 hours.
data.limits: 40 hours per 25-month biennial compliance period; 3 hours must be ethics. Up to 50% of excess CE may carry forward. Independent study has no stated separate cap, but all hours must satisfy the rule's standards and proof requirements.
data.passage: 481—881.1: 'Independent study' ... 'includes a posttest and meets the general criteria in subrule 881.2(9).' 481—881.2(9)(a)-(e): activity must be organized learning, practice-related, conducted by qualified individuals, fulfill goals/objectives, and provide proof including contact hours and a certificate. 481—881.2(10)(a)(3): 'Independent study courses that meet the general criteria in subrule 881.2(9).' 481—881.2(1): minimum 40 hours; 881.2(10)(b)(1): three hours ethics.

data.providerPathway: Conditional: Iowa's current behavioral-health rule does not name NBCC-approved providers as an automatic provider pathway. An NBCC-provider course can qualify only conditionally if the course/activity independently satisfies 481—881.2(9)'s content, instructor, objective, and certificate/proof standards; the rule expressly lists acceptable activity types but not NBCC providership.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous/home-study is accepted as an 'independent study course' if it meets 481—881.2(9), and the definition requires a posttest. No separate home-study cap or special hour conversion is stated; the renewal requirement is 40 hours per biennium.
data.limits: 40 hours per 25-month biennial compliance period; 3 hours ethics; 3 hours supervision for licensees serving in a supervisory role. Up to 50% of excess CE may carry forward. The rule provides no separate cap for independent study/home study.
data.passage: 481—881.2(10)(a)(1)-(3): credit may be obtained through workshops/conferences/symposiums/webinars, academic courses, and 'Independent study courses that meet the general criteria in subrule 881.2(9).' 481—881.2(9)(c)-(e): qualified presenters, stated goals/objectives, and certificate/proof with contact hours. 481—881.2(1): minimum 40 hours; 881.2(10)(b)(1): three ethics hours.

data.providerPathway: Unsupported as an NBCC-provider pathway: Iowa's social-work rule expressly identifies ASWB Approved Continuing Education (ACE) and NASW CEU Approval, not NBCC. A course may still be creditable if it meets the independent general criteria and required social-work content, but NBCC providership alone is not identified as qualifying.
data.asyncRule: The cited current social-work rule does not expressly use 'home study,' 'asynchronous,' or 'independent study' as a specific pathway. It requires an organized learning activity, qualified instructor, objectives, proof/certificate, and specified social-work content; therefore asynchronous acceptance is unresolved from this rule rather than assumed.
data.limits: 27 hours per two-year biennium, including at least 3 hours of social-work ethics. No general home-study/asynchronous cap or hour calculation is stated. Licensees must retain CE documentation; no carryover is allowed under 896.2(5).
data.passage: 481—896.3(1)(a)-(f): creditable activity must be organized learning, practice-related, conducted by qualified individuals, meet objectives, provide certificate/proof, and contain a listed social-work content area. 481—896.3(2)(d)(1)-(2): activities sponsored/approved by '(1) ASWB Approved Continuing Education (ACE) program; or (2) National Association of Social Workers (NASW) Continuing Education Unit (CEU) Approval Program.' 481—896.2(1): minimum 27 hours; 896.3(2)(a): minimum 3 ethics hours; 896.2(5): no carryover.

data.providerPathway: CONDITIONAL: Maine does not state that NBCC approval alone qualifies or require separate provider registration. The rule permits CE offered by accredited-institution departments, national/state/local professional organizations, public/private human-services organizations, private consultants, or individuals; an NBCC ACEP course is therefore usable only if it independently satisfies Maine's content and documentation rules.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous online/home study is accepted. Formal home-study and online/internet/distance-learning programs have no stated maximum; informal home study or prerecorded programs are capped at 5 contact hours combined. Courses must relate directly to counseling theory/practice and be documented.
data.limits: 55 contact hours per biennium: up to 15 peer consultation, at least 4 ethics, remaining hours counseling theory/practice. Graduate academic distance learning and formal home study/online/distance learning: no maximum. Informal home study/prerecorded: 5-hour maximum. Same prerecorded/home-study/distance program may not be claimed more than once.
data.passage: Board Rule 514 CMR Chapter 7-A §3: “Continuing education activities ... may be offered by departments of accredited institutions ... [or] private consultants or individuals”; “formal home study courses and on line, internet and other distance learning programs” must be documented. §3(3): formal home study/online/distance learning “No maximum”; §3(4): “Up to five contact hours for informal home study or prerecorded programs, combined.” §1: 55 contact hours, including at least four ethics hours.

data.providerPathway: CONDITIONAL: The Maine counseling board's LMFT (MF) renewal rule does not identify NBCC approval as a standalone approval pathway or require provider registration. NBCC-provider courses can qualify only when the course is directly related to professional counseling theory/practice and meets Maine documentation requirements.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous online/home study is accepted under the same Chapter 7-A rule applicable to the MF license: formal home study and online/internet/distance learning have no stated maximum; informal home study or prerecorded programs are capped at 5 contact hours combined.
data.limits: 55 contact hours per biennium; at least 4 ethics hours; up to 15 peer-consultation hours; remaining hours must concern counseling theory/practice. Formal home study/online/distance learning: no maximum. Informal home study/prerecorded: maximum 5 combined; no duplicate credit for the same program.
data.passage: Board Rule 514 CMR Chapter 7-A §3: “formal home study courses, and on line, internet and other distance learning programs” are eligible and have “No maximum”; §3(4): “Up to five contact hours for informal home study or prerecorded programs, combined.” §1: licensees attest to 55 hours and §2 requires at least four hours on the Code of Ethics. The Board page lists MF renewal as 55 hours under Chapter 7-A.

data.providerPathway: CONDITIONAL: Maine's social-work rule does not name NBCC approval as sufficient and does not require a separate CE-provider registration. NBCC-approved-provider material is potentially usable only if it is directly related to social-work practice and fits the rule's activity, interaction, and documentation requirements; NBCC approval by itself is not enough under the text.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous/noninteractive online or virtual education is accepted, but it is in the capped category: at least 15 of the 25 hours must provide immediate instructor interaction, and no more than 10 hours total may come from activities where immediate interaction is unavailable plus teaching/writing/independent-study activities. Independent study may be claimed only once for a particular course and not if substantially similar to a course already taken for credit in the same renewal period.
data.limits: 25 contact hours per biennial term, directly related to social-work practice; for LCSW (not conditional LSX), at least 4 hours ethics. At least 15 hours must have immediate instructor interaction. Maximum 10 hours total from noninteractive activities (subsection 2) and subsection 3 activities. Family/intimate-partner-violence coursework applies if required by statute.
data.passage: Board Rule 416 CMR Chapter 14 §1: “25 contact hours ... directly related to the practice of social work”; for all other licensees “at least 4 ... in social work ethics.” §3: “At least 15 hours” must have “immediate interaction with the instructor”; “A maximum of 10 hours total” is allowed where immediate interaction is unavailable and in §3(3). §3(C): independent-study credit may be claimed “only once for a particular course.”

data.providerPathway: NBCC is an expressly listed deemed-approved organization for LMHC programs; an NBCC-approved provider's program can qualify without separate Indiana board preapproval, provided the program is relevant to the licensee's practice and meets the rule's provider/program standards (objectives, qualified faculty, evaluation, and attendance record).
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous home study is accepted as Category I, including computer, audio, and video home-study programs. The rule does not impose a separate asynchronous-hour cap; Category I must supply at least 50% of renewal CEUs and Category II may supply no more than 50%.
data.limits: LMHC renewal requires 20 CEUs per year (40 per two-year renewal). At least 50% must be Category I (therefore at least 10/year or 20/renewal period); Category II is capped at 50%. Category I credit equals the hours granted by the sponsor, or one CEU per clock hour if the sponsor grants no hours. One Category I CEU per year must be ethics/professional conduct, including boundary issues.
data.passage: 839 IAC 1-6-1(b): licensee shall obtain a minimum of fifty percent of required CEUs from Category I and may obtain a maximum of fifty percent from Category II; 839 IAC 1-6-1(c)(6): Category I includes home study programs, including computer, audio, and video. 839 IAC 1-6-2(f)(53): programs sponsored, accredited, or approved by the National Board for Certified Counselors are deemed approved. 839 IAC 1-6-2(a)(1),(4)-(8): objectives must relate to/enhance practice; curriculum must concern the licensee's practice; qualified faculty, evaluation, and meaningful attendance record are required. 839 IAC 1-6-2(b): organizations applying for board approval submit an application 90 days before presentation. 839 IAC 1-6-2(d)-(e): attendance must be reliably verified and records retained four years. 839 IAC 1-6-2(b), (c): approval expires April 1 of even-numbered years. 839 IAC 1-6-2 (renewal subsection): 20 CEUs per year, 40 for two-year renewal.

data.providerPathway: NBCC-sponsored or NBCC-approved general continuing-education programs are approved without further board review. The program still must be directly related to professional growth and development of professional-counseling practice; mandatory domestic-violence, suicide, and Kentucky-law trainings require Board approval.
data.asyncRule: The regulation does not expressly address asynchronous/home-study or online delivery in the current provider-approval/delivery provisions; therefore acceptance of a generic asynchronous course is unresolved (NBCC status alone does not establish an async rule).
data.limits: 10 CE hours per annual renewal period; all hours must be in or related to professional counseling. No asynchronous/home-study cap or hour-calculation rule is stated in the fetched regulation.
data.passage: 201 KAR 36:030, Sections 1(1)-(2), 2(1)(a)3, 2(1): “A minimum of ten (10) continuing education hours” and programs “Sponsored or approved by ... The National Board for Certified Counselors” are approved “without further review by the board.” Section 3 requires course description, instructor qualifications, agenda, hours, certificate, and evaluation for board approval.

data.providerPathway: NBCC is not listed as an automatically accepted provider pathway. Programs by other organizations, educational institutions, or service providers require Kentucky LMFT Board review/approval; approval depends on organized learning, relevant MFT subject matter, professional competency, and relevant instructor training/experience. A provider/sponsor seeking approval must apply in advance and submit course/provider materials; sponsor approval is a separate pathway for multiple programs.
data.asyncRule: Online study courses are expressly contemplated, but are in the category of programs requiring Board review and possible approval. The rule does not state a separate asynchronous/home-study cap or hour-conversion formula.
data.limits: 15 approved CE hours per annual renewal for a licensee, including 3 hours MFT ethics; 6 suicide-assessment hours every 6 years (unless otherwise counted under the rule). Presenter credit is full contact-hour credit but capped at one-half of renewal requirements; publication credit is one-half of required renewal hours.
data.passage: 201 KAR 32:060, Sections 1(1)-(3), 2(1)-(2), 3(1)-(3): “a minimum of fifteen (15) approved continuing education hours”; online study courses are among programs that “shall be reviewed and may be determined to be relevant”; a provider applies “at least sixty (60) days in advance” with type, subject matter, instructor qualifications, and hours, while sponsors submit a sample course, delivery format, certificate, and procedures.

data.providerPathway: NBCC-sponsored programs are listed among preapproved sources (alongside professional associations and other listed sponsors), so the provider pathway can qualify for general renewal CE when the program is relevant to social work and contributes to continuing professional competency. Provider/sponsor approval is not required for those preapproved sources, but the certificate/documentation and content standards still apply; special ethics and clinical-supervision courses are not automatically preapproved.
data.asyncRule: Home/self-study and electronic-media courses (including distance learning, online, and teleconference) are accepted methods. If not from a preapproved source, Board approval must be obtained each year; the fetched regulation states no numeric home-study/online cap or different hour calculation.
data.limits: 15 CE hours per 3-year renewal period for an LS; 30 hours for a CSW/LCSW. Licensee-presented programs are full contact-hour credit but limited to one-half of renewal requirements. No numeric asynchronous cap is stated in the current fetched text.
data.passage: 201 KAR 23:075, Sections 2(1)(b)3, 3(2)(a)-(c), 4(1)-(3): NBCC is a listed sponsor; the Board “may approve various methods” including “Home or self-study, courses delivered through electronic media or technology including distance learning, online, or teleconference”; approval “shall be obtained each year” unless the program is exempt, and provider applications require objectives, instructor CVs, evaluation, agenda, hours, and certificate.

data.providerPathway: Unresolved from the current official rule: IDAPA 24.15.01.100.07 states required CE subject areas but does not state that an NBCC-approved CE provider pathway qualifies for general renewal credit, nor set a provider-approval/registration route.
data.asyncRule: Unresolved in the current counselor rule. The official Board CE page directs licensees to Rule 100.07, whose published text contains no home-study, online, asynchronous, or distance-learning provision.
data.limits: Unresolved from the current official counselor rule. Rule 100.07 specifies 6 ethics hours, 3 boundaries hours, and 3 suicide-assessment/intervention hours per 24-month period, but the fetched text does not state a total CE-hour requirement, asynchronous cap, or hour calculation.
data.passage: IDAPA 24.15.01.100.07: "In each twenty-four (24) month period preceding the renewal of a license, all licensees must complete six (6) hours in ethics, three (3) hours of boundaries, and three (3) hours in suicide assessment or intervention."

data.providerPathway: Unresolved from the current official rule: IDAPA 24.15.01.100.07 states required CE subject areas but does not state that an NBCC-approved CE provider pathway qualifies for general renewal credit, nor set a provider-approval/registration route.
data.asyncRule: Unresolved in the current marriage-and-family-therapy rule. The official Board CE page directs licensees to Rule 100.07, whose published text contains no home-study, online, asynchronous, or distance-learning provision.
data.limits: Unresolved from the current official rule. Rule 100.07 specifies 6 ethics hours, 3 boundaries hours, and 3 suicide-assessment/intervention hours per 24-month period, but the fetched text does not state a total CE-hour requirement, asynchronous cap, or hour calculation.
data.passage: IDAPA 24.15.01.100.07: "In each twenty-four (24) month period preceding the renewal of a license, all licensees must complete six (6) hours in ethics, three (3) hours of boundaries, and three (3) hours in suicide assessment or intervention."

data.providerPathway: Unresolved: the current official social-work rule does not identify NBCC-approved CE providers as a qualifying provider pathway or require/register an additional provider. The Board expressly says it does not pre-approve courses.
data.asyncRule: Online/asynchronous courses are accepted if germane to social-work practice. The official Board FAQ does not impose a separate asynchronous cap or distinguish synchronous from asynchronous delivery.
data.limits: 30 CE hours during each preceding 24 months; 2 hours must be professional ethics and the remainder germane to social-work practice; no carryover for excess hours. No asynchronous-specific cap or hour-conversion formula is stated. Proof must be retained 4 years.
data.passage: IDAPA 24.14.01.100.05: "licensees must complete during the preceding twenty-four (24) months ... thirty (30) hours of continuing education, two (2) hours of which must be in professional ethics and the remainder germane to the practice of social work." Board FAQ: "Yes, online courses germane to the practice of social work are allowable."

data.providerPathway: CONDITIONAL: COMAR 10.58.05.07B(2) automatically approves a program sponsored by NBCC for Category A, but the rule does not expressly say that an NBCC-approved CE provider (ACEP) pathway, by itself, makes every provider's course automatically approved. Otherwise the sponsor must be Board-approved/authorized. Course scope remains required: professional mental-health audience, stated purpose/defined content, qualified presenters, completion documentation and evaluation (10.58.05.05A(1)(a)(ii)-(viii)); content must meet 10.58.05.04A objectives.
data.asyncRule: Ordinary home study is expressly excluded from CE (10.58.05.04B(3)); self-paced/distance learning can be Category B only when it has evidence of appropriateness, minimum mastery, and completion (10.58.05.06A(3)).
data.limits: 40 CEUs per 2-year renewal: at least 30 Category A and no more than 10 Category B, or all 40 Category A (10.58.05.03A). One CEU is 60 minutes (10.58.05.02(8)); no separate asynchronous hour conversion is stated.
data.passage: 10.58.05.07B(2): “A program sponsored by ... the National Board for Certified Counselors ... is automatically approved by the Board for Category A”; 10.58.05.04B(3): “Home study”; 10.58.05.06A(3): “distance learning programs with evidence of appropriateness, minimum mastery of materials, and completion.”

data.providerPathway: CONDITIONAL: The same COMAR 10.58.05 chapter expressly covers marriage and family therapists. NBCC-sponsored programs are automatically Category A under 10.58.05.07B(2), but an NBCC-approved-provider designation alone is not expressly identified as automatic approval. Non-automatic sponsors need Board authorization; course content/instructor/completion/evaluation standards apply.
data.asyncRule: Home study is excluded. Distance learning is potentially accepted as Category B if appropriateness, minimum mastery, and completion are documented; a bare asynchronous home-study course is not accepted under the definition/exclusion.
data.limits: 40 CEUs each renewal period: minimum 30 Category A and maximum 10 Category B, or 40 Category A (10.58.05.03A); 1 CEU = 60 minutes (10.58.05.02(8)).
data.passage: 10.58.05.07B(2): “the National Board for Certified Counselors ... is automatically approved ... for Category A”; 10.58.05.05A(1)(a): “Presenters are professionals qualified in the defined content area”; 10.58.05.06A(3): “minimum mastery of materials, and completion.”

data.providerPathway: CONDITIONAL/UNRESOLVED for NBCC: Maryland social-work rules require approved programs to be under an authorized sponsor (10.42.06.02(1)-(2)). NBCC is not listed among the specifically named automatic authorized sponsors in 10.42.06.05A(2); a relevant non-social-work organization may qualify only within the rule's authorized-sponsor framework. The Board requires sponsor content/objectives, certificate and records standards; no rule found that an NBCC-approved-provider pathway alone suffices.
data.asyncRule: Accepted: online learning by a Board-authorized sponsor expressly includes “Webinar, pre-recorded and non-interactive,” “Online course,” “Distance learning,” and “Home study course” (10.42.06.04E(7)). For a home-study certificate gap, proof of completion such as a post-test passing score or other Board-satisfactory proof is required (10.42.06.06C(4)(e)).
data.limits: 40 CEUs per 2-year period (30 for LBSW); at least 20 Category I; maximum 20 Category II (15 for LBSW) (10.42.06.03A; 10.42.06.04E). Any 60-minute contact/clock/hour is 1 CEU (10.42.06.04C(3)); no separate online cap beyond Category II maximum is stated.
data.passage: 10.42.06.04E(7): “Online learning provided by a Board-authorized sponsor, such as ... Webinar, pre-recorded and non-interactive ... Distance learning; and ... Home study course”; 10.42.06.05A(4)(a)-(b): certificate must state objectives/content, CEUs, authorized sponsor and sponsor responsibility.

data.providerPathway: The current Kansas LPC rule does not identify an NBCC-approved CE-provider pathway or require provider registration. Credit is tied to documented, approved continuing education and qualifying content; the activity must enhance professional-counseling practice, values, ethics, skills, or knowledge. NBCC-provider recognition is therefore unresolved from the official rule.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous home study is expressly accepted: a computerized interactive learning module, telecast/videotape, audiotape, or reading qualifies. With a posttest, up to 30 hours may be counted; without a posttest, up to 5 hours.
data.limits: 30 hours every two-year renewal period; at least 3 ethics hours and 6 diagnosis-and-treatment hours. One hour is at least 50 minutes of instructor-participant classroom instruction or an actual hour of another acceptable experience; no credit under 15 minutes. Excess hours do not carry over.
data.passage: K.A.R. 102-3-10a(a): "Each licensee shall complete 30 hours of documented and approved continuing education oriented to the enhancement of a professional counselor's practice, values, ethics, skills, or knowledge"; (d)(4)-(5): home-study media with a posttest has a 30-hour maximum, and without a posttest a five-hour maximum.

data.providerPathway: The current Kansas LMFT rule does not identify an NBCC-approved CE-provider pathway or require provider registration. Credit is tied to approved programs and qualifying content; the activity must enhance marriage-and-family-therapy practice, ethics, values, skills, or knowledge. NBCC-provider recognition is unresolved from the official rule.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous home study is expressly accepted: a computerized interactive learning module, telecast/videotape, audiotape, or reading qualifies. With a posttest, up to 40 hours may be counted; without a posttest, up to 10 hours.
data.limits: 40 hours every two-year renewal period; at least 3 formal ethics hours and 6 formal diagnosis-and-treatment hours. Credit is based on actual contact time; 15 to under 25 minutes earns one-quarter hour, and less than 15 minutes earns no credit. Excess hours do not carry over.
data.passage: K.A.R. 102-5-10(a): "Each licensee shall complete 40 hours of documented and approved continuing education"; (e)(4)-(5): home-study media with a posttest has a 40-hour maximum, and without a posttest a 10-hour maximum.

data.providerPathway: NBCC approval alone is not stated as a qualifying Kansas pathway. Kansas instead provides an approved-provider pathway: the provider applies to the board, pays the fee, submits an organizational plan and systems for records/instructors/participant requirements, and documents program content, objectives, format, instructor qualifications, evaluation, and agenda. A single-program provider is another board-application route. Extra Kansas provider approval/registration is required for those pathways.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous home study is expressly accepted. If a posttest is provided, up to 40 hours may count; without a posttest, up to 10 hours. A program presented by an approved program provider may count up to 40 hours.
data.limits: 40 units every two-year renewal period; at least 3 ethics units and (for LMSW/LCSW) at least 6 diagnosis-and-treatment units. One unit is at least 50 minutes of classroom instruction or an actual hour of another acceptable experience. Approved-provider and single-program-provider activities each have a 40-hour maximum; excess units do not carry over.
data.passage: K.A.R. 102-2-4b(b)(2)-(5): an approved-provider applicant must submit an organizational plan and develop record, instructor, participant, and program-documentation systems; K.A.R. 102-2-4a(e)(4)-(5): home study with a posttest is capped at 40 hours and without one at 10 hours.

data.providerPathway: Supported: CE approved by NBCC is accepted for general renewal credit. The activity must be in one of the 14 approved content areas; the rule says the Board does not preapprove CE from providers without listed provider status, but reviews it at renewal and requires a qualified presenter.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous/home-study credit is accepted. The rule expressly includes journals, video presentations, and webinars as home-study options, and requires a provider number from NBCC, ACA, LCA, or another board-approved mental-health organization.
data.limits: 40 CEHs every two-year renewal period; maximum 20 CEHs online (except regionally accredited higher-education coursework); home study maximum 10 hours per renewal period. One CEH equals one clock hour. Home-study verification is a qualifying certificate and the activity specifies CEHs.
data.passage: LAC 46: LX §707.B.2.a: ‘continuing education that is approved by ... the National Board of Certified Counselors (NBCC) will be accepted by the Board of Examiners.’ §707.B.2.d: ‘Home Study (10 hours maximum per renewal period)’ and each option ‘must carry a provider number from either NBCC, ACA, LCA, or other board-approved mental health organizations’; §707.B.2: ‘a maximum of 20 CEHs may be obtained through an online format’; §707.B.2.b: ‘The board will not preapprove any type of continuing education’ and content must be in §707.C and given by a qualified presenter.

data.providerPathway: Conditional: The LMFT rule expressly names LCA, AAMFT and its regional/state divisions (including LAMFT) as provider pathways, but does not expressly name NBCC. CE from an organization without provider status is reviewed by the advisory committee at renewal, with relevant content and a qualified presenter required; therefore an NBCC-provider pathway is not automatic under the fetched rule.
data.asyncRule: Online CE is accepted, but the fetched LMFT rule does not separately define or identify asynchronous home-study delivery for LMFTs. It states only the online-format cap; whether a particular asynchronous NBCC home-study activity qualifies is therefore subject to the renewal-time approval pathway and is unresolved from this rule.
data.limits: 40 clock hours every two-year renewal period; maximum 20 CEHs online (except regionally accredited higher-education coursework). Required within the 40: 3 hours LMFT-specific ethics, 6 hours diagnosis, and 3 hours social/cultural foundations; at least 20 hours must be MFT/systemic content when counting another license's CE. One CEU equals one clock hour.
data.passage: LAC 46: LX §3503.C.1: ‘a maximum of 20 CEHs may be obtained through an online format’; §3503.C.1.a.i names ‘the Louisiana Counseling Association (LCA), the American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy (AAMFT) and its regional or state divisions including ... LAMFT’; §3503.C.1.a.iii: organizations ‘not holding provider status ... will be subject to approval ... at the time of renewal’ and ‘The advisory committee will not pre-approve any type of continuing education.’

data.providerPathway: Conditional: The current official administrative code lists social-work licensing bodies, Board-authorized pre-approval organizations, professional social-work organizations, CSWE schools, and ASWB-approved entities; it does not name NBCC. An NBCC-provider course may potentially be submitted if its content is applicable to social-work practice and the licensee retains the course materials and certificate, but automatic NBCC-provider acceptance is not established.
data.asyncRule: Asynchronous virtual learning—including teleconferences, telecourses, home-study and prerecorded/internet courses—is accepted when sponsored by the listed entities or pre-approved by a Board-authorized pre-approval organization, provided the content applies to social-work practice. Synchronous interactive webinars are treated as in-person learning.
data.limits: 20 CE hours annually for renewal; no more than 10 hours via asynchronous virtual learning/teaching in a collection period. The Board may approve more than 10 hours for documented disability/travel impossibility, residence outside U.S. territories without available in-person CE, or other good cause. Content-applicable materials and certificate must be retained for audit.
data.passage: LAC 46:XXV §1305.A.3: ‘asynchronous virtual learning (teleconferences, telecourses, home-study courses and pre-recorded or internet courses)’ is approved when sponsored by listed entities or pre-approved, and ‘cannot exceed ... 10 clock hours’ of the required 20 annually; §1313.A: ‘Social workers may not submit more than ten hours ... via asynchronous virtual learning’; §1305.B requires the Guide, course materials and certificate when an offering is not pre-approved.

data.providerPathway: Conditional/unresolved: 262 CMR 7.02 defines eligible providers as 'Entity-approved Sponsors' approved by Board-recognized entities; the regulation does not say that NBCC Approved Continuing Education Provider status by itself is a qualifying pathway. Any course must be within the Board-recognized entity's approved scope and meet its delivery procedures.
data.asyncRule: Unresolved from the official regulation: 262 CMR 7.00 does not expressly address asynchronous, online, distance, or home-study delivery. It requires a contact hour to be an organized learning experience lasting 50 consecutive minutes and requires official verification of attendance.
data.limits: 30 contact hours per two-year licensure/renewal period; one contact hour is 50 consecutive minutes. No asynchronous/home-study cap or hour-conversion rule is stated in 262 CMR 7.00.
data.passage: 262 CMR 7.02: 'Entity-approved Sponsors. Continuing education providers that have been approved by Board-Recognized Entities'; 'Contact Hour. The unit of measurement for an organized learning experience lasting 50 consecutive minutes.' 262 CMR 7.03(1): 'minimum of 30 Contact Hours ... per licensure/renewal period (every two years).' 262 CMR 7.04(2)(f): 'official verification of attendance'.

data.providerPathway: Conditional/unresolved: LMFTs are governed by 262 CMR 7.00. NBCC Approved Continuing Education Provider status is not named in that regulation as automatic approval; provider/course acceptance depends on approval by a Board-recognized entity and its content/delivery procedures.
data.asyncRule: Unresolved from the official regulation: no express asynchronous, online, distance, or home-study rule appears in 262 CMR 7.00. The stated measurement is an organized learning experience of 50 consecutive minutes, with official attendance verification.
data.limits: 30 contact hours per two-year licensure/renewal period; 50 consecutive minutes per contact hour. No online/home-study cap or asynchronous calculation is specified in the cited official regulation.
data.passage: 262 CMR 7.02: 'Entities may define continuing education content areas appropriate for the specific license' and 'may define procedures for the sponsors to follow in the delivery'; 262 CMR 7.03(1): 'minimum of 30 Contact Hours ... every two years.'

data.providerPathway: Supported only conditionally and limited: 258 CMR 31.04(5) expressly lists NBCC among organizations whose approved courses may receive credit, but only up to 25% of required CE and only if the program contributes to professional competence in social work. At least 75% must be from a recognized-entity pathway. The provider/course must also satisfy content and administrative requirements, including qualified presenters, licensed-professional involvement, comprehension, certificate timing, and a recognized-entity authorization number.
data.asyncRule: Unresolved from the official regulation: 258 CMR 31.00 does not expressly identify asynchronous/online/home-study delivery or provide a special cap/calculation for it. Any course must meet the general 50-minute CE-hour rule and approval/documentation requirements.
data.limits: LCSW: 30 CE hours per licensure period (258 CMR 31.03(1)(a)); at least 75% must be approved by a recognized entity; NBCC-approved courses fall in the 'up to 25%' other-organizations category, so ordinarily up to 7.5 hours of a 30-hour period, subject to professional-competence and course requirements. Each CE hour is at least 50 minutes of actual instruction time.
data.passage: 258 CMR 31.04(5): 'A licensee may receive up to 25% of continuing education credit' and the Board-approved list includes '(b) National Board for Certified Counselors (NBCC)'; 'All licensees must receive a minimum of 75%'. 258 CMR 31.03(1)(a): 'Licensed Independent Clinical Social Workers (LICSWs) – 30 continuing education hours' [the regulation uses LICSW, not LCSW, for the 30-hour level]. 258 CMR 31.04(3)(b): 'at least 50 consecutive minutes in length'.
